title: Cu2WSe4: orbital versus spin Edelstein response of a gyrotropic achiral crystal

decision_points.fork: Point group and axes: the staged CIF is written in P1; the D2d operations must be found from the coordinates, with the twofold axes along a and b (I-42m setting), not on the diagonals
decision_points.wrong_choice: Assume the -4m2 setting (mirrors along a, b) or a chiral class
decision_points.consequence: allowed Edelstein components ['xy', 'yx'] and nonlinear components ['xxz', 'xzx', 'yyz', 'yzy', 'zxx', 'zyy'] instead of ['xx', 'yy'] and ['xyz', 'xzy', 'yxz', 'yzx', 'zxy', 'zyx']

decision_points.fork: Orbital-moment operator: the wave-packet moment with the Wannier-centre position operator is the Berry-phase moment; the service also offers the intra-atomic -mu_B<L>
decision_points.wrong_choice: Use the intra-atomic (atomic L) moment, or add it to the Berry-phase moment (both dev pilots did the latter: CB ratio -2.75)
decision_points.consequence: orbital/spin 0.266 (VB) and -2.41 (CB) instead of -11.2 and -0.339: both conclusions reversed

decision_points.fork: The no-SOC model has 54 spinless Wannier functions (header: collinear, spinsize 1): every state counts twice for the crystal in alpha
decision_points.wrong_choice: Use the model sum as the crystal response

decision_points.fork: Rigid-band hole counting in the spinless model (cascade: mu(p) then alpha); the two errors partly cancel
decision_points.wrong_choice: Count one hole per band and k-point of the spinless model
decision_points.consequence: ratio 0.464 (or 0.928 with both spin factors omitted)

decision_points.fork: Energy reference: the header Fermi levels of the two models lie mid-gap at different distances from the band edges (VBM -0.599 vs -0.644 eV); the paper compares the models on that common axis
decision_points.wrong_choice: Compare the models at the same mu on the header scale instead of at equal hole density

decision_points.fork: Mesh convergence: the orbital terms converge by N = 24-32, but the small valence-edge spin term keeps drifting to the densest meshes; a mesh that looks converged for the orbital part is not converged for the ratio
decision_points.wrong_choice: Stop at the 32 mesh (1 unit) because M_orb is stable

decision_points.fork: Units and relaxation time: gamma = hbar/(2 tau), q = -|e|, sums per cell of the model divided by the conventional-cell volume
decision_points.wrong_choice: tau = hbar/gamma, or a positive carrier charge

decision_points.fork: Valence versus conduction band: W-d spin-orbit coupling makes spin dominate at the conduction-band edge
decision_points.wrong_choice: Transfer the valence-band conclusion (orbital dominance) to the conduction band

decision_points.fork: Nonlinear Hall relation: for the Berry-curvature dipole D_xx = -D_yy, D_zz = 0 give sigma_zxy = -2 sigma_xyz
decision_points.wrong_choice: Assume full index-permutation symmetry of sigma_ijl (sigma_zxy = sigma_xyz)

decision_points.fork: Chirality indicator: tr G vanishes for the achiral, strongly gyrotropic class D2d
decision_points.wrong_choice: Treat the gyrotropic crystal as chiral (alpha_yy = alpha_xx)
decision_points.consequence: chirality indicator 2 and alpha_yy/alpha_xx = +1 instead of 0 and -1

graded_fields: orbital_to_spin_ratio at VBM-0.10 and CBM+0.10 eV (SOC model), each within 25%
orbital_magnetization_A_per_m (M_x, VBM-0.10 eV, E_x = 1e4 V/m, gamma = 30 meV) within 15%
edelstein_allowed_components == [xx, yy]; alpha_yy/alpha_xx = -1 and chirality indicator = 0 (+-0.05)
nonlinear_hall_allowed_components == [xyz, xzy, yxz, yzx, zxy, zyx]; sigma_zxy/sigma_xyz = -2 (+-0.15)

length_estimate.catalog_units: fermi_surface meshes 16-128 cost 24 units (soc) + 14 units (nosoc) = 38, plus any number of bands / band_properties requests (1 unit each)
length_estimate.why: Symmetry analysis from a P1 CIF, band-edge location in two models, choice of orbital operator, a mesh study of a slowly converging spin term under a binding budget, rigid-band counting in a spinless model and a cascade into the SOC comparison, unit conversion of the Boltzmann response, and the BCD relation.

runtime_dependencies: numpy and scipy (runtime image); no extra layer
notes: Graded values come from the validated evaluator, not directly from the archive: the archived orbital Edelstein curves equal -2 x the paper-convention (wave-packet) orbital response, while the archived spin curve matches the evaluator in absolute units (scale 1.002). Nonlinear Hall magnitudes are not graded (BCD at kT = 10 meV is dominated by near-degeneracy hot spots and the archive differs by a convention factor ~2); only exact symmetry relations are. The valence-edge orbital/spin ratio carries a mesh uncertainty (128 mesh -11.2, 1/N extrapolation -13.4), covered by the 25% window.
